title: fix(sse): streaming chunking & framing - handle partial JSON, delimiter edgecases, and token/event ordering
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Fixes SSE streaming framing bugs: partial JSON chunks and delimiter handling to prevent malformed events during streaming; improves token/event ordering and adds tests.
body:
Context and motivation: We have recurring customer reports and internal flaky tests showing malformed SSE events for long streaming responses, especially when: 1) the model emits partial JSON (function/tool calling / structured output) that spans multiple tokens/events, 2) the framing delimiter ("\n\n") was split across network chunks, and 3) edge ordering cases where a token boundary and an SSE event boundary overlap. These issues cause downstream parsers (OpenAI-compat clients and our SDKs) to receive invalid JSON or non-deterministic event ordering.

What this PR does: - Robustly handle partial JSON emitted by the model by buffering incomplete JSON fragments across SSE chunks and only emitting complete JSON events. - Fix delimiter detection so event separators that are split across network/chunk boundaries are recognized. - Preserve token->event ordering by making the framer deterministic when reassembling chunks from multiple goroutines / read loops. - Add defensive checks and metrics to make regressions visible (sse.framer.malformed_count, sse.framer.buffer_bytes). - Add unit + integration tests that simulate split delimiters and large structured output streaming.

Checklist: - [x] Tests added for split-delimiter and partial-JSON scenarios - [x] Added metric and log for malformed reassembly - [x] Verified with python/ts SDK examples - [x] CI passes after flakiness fixes

Commits (summary): - 9f3b2c8: sse: add Framer state machine to buffer partial events and reassemble delimiters reliably - a7d6f11: sse: fix race in chunk queue ordering when reader yields empty chunks - 3cbe4dd: sse: add tests for split-delimiter and partial-json - d439e20: openai-compat: ensure structured output path waits for complete JSON block - b12a4e6: docs: note SSE framing guarantees in streaming API docs

Files changed (high level): - sse/framer.go: new state machine + buffering logic (main fix) - sse/framer_test.go: new tests for split delimiter and partial JSON - transport/http_stream.go: integrate Framer into HTTP reader path and preserve ordering - openai/compat_stream.go: compatibility layer waiting logic to avoid early emission of incomplete structured outputs - sdk/python/examples/streaming_json.py: test harness updated to use test vector - docs/api/streaming.md: added framing guarantees and migration notes - metrics/registry.go: added sse.framer.* metrics - go.mod: bumped test deps

Small illustrative change (framer algorithm): previously we searched for delimiter ("\n\n") in each chunk and emitted events independently. That logic failed when delimiter split across chunks. New approach: maintain a small sliding buffer of last k bytes, append incoming chunk, scan for delimiter across the concatenated buffer, extract complete events, and keep remainder as pending fragment. The framer also tracks whether the current event is expected to be JSON (based on last-sent content-type hint) and will attempt to validate JSON completeness before emitting.

Review conversation (high level): - Miguel Alvarez (reviewer): "This looks sound; two questions: 1) how expensive is the repeated scanning for severe high-throughput paths? and 2) any risk of unbounded buffering?" - Asha (author): "We cap the buffer to 64KB by default and emit a telemetry counter when exceeded; scanning cost is linear on new bytes and the delimiter is small. Benchmarks show <2% CPU increase at 10k req/s for a single framer. Added the limit/metric per suggestion." - Ivy Zhang: "Add a test that simulates delimiter split with a 1-byte boundary and verify ordering with multiple concurrent readers." - Asha: "Added test and the transport path now serializes framer emission per-connection to preserve ordering; see transport/http_stream.go change." - Connor Reed: "Approve after small nit on variable naming and a comment about potential edgecases when content-type hint is missing." - Connor Reed: "LGTM" (approved).

CI and testing notes: - Initial CI run (linux/amd64 unit tests) failed because of a flakey test relying on timing in framer_test.go; fixed by switching to deterministic synchronization and re-ran CI. - Integration tests (streaming smoke) were added and passed in the second run. - CI checks: build: pass, unit-tests: pass (after fix), integration-tests: pass, lint: pass.

Backward compatibility and migration: - No API contract changes. Behavior is stricter: clients that previously relied on receiving partial JSON events will now get full JSON objects (recommended). SDKs updated with compatibility behavior; older clients will not break but may see slightly delayed first event for structured outputs.

Release notes (short): Fix SSE streaming framing bugs: correct handling of partial JSON and split delimiters; increases streaming stability for tool/function calling and structured output flows.

Notes for on-call / SRE: - If you see sse.framer.malformed_count > 0 spike, check recent traffic shapes and test vector failure logs in /var/log/redwood/sse-framer.log. - Buffer cap is 64KB (configurable via REDWOOD_SSE_FRAMER_MAX_BUFFER).

Related: ENG-4820 (streaming stability), ENG-4915 (openai-compat structured output), previous PRs pr-18234-sse-streaming-chunking-framing-fixes.json and similar followups.

Merge details: Squash-merged into main after approvals and green CI.
